options.D: The virus rapidly destroys red blood cells and causes severe systemic anemia

explanation: High-risk HPV can change cervical cells without causing any pain or warning signs. That's why routine Pap smears are so lifesaving!

question: How should a good QA committee handle mistakes in the hospital?

options.A: Hide medical errors from the public and media
options.B: Punish staff members immediately when something goes wrong
options.C: Find the root cause and prevent the mistake from happening again
options.D: Focus only on financial losses after an incident

explanation: Brilliant! Modern healthcare focuses on fixing the system so mistakes don't repeat, rather than just blaming people.

question: A patient with severe malaria is admitted to your ward. How should they first receive their medication?

options.A: Oral tablets swallowed with water
options.B: Subcutaneous daily injection
options.C: Rectal suppositories only
options.D: Intravenous or intramuscular

explanation: Well done! Severe cases move fast, so we need fast-acting injections (IV or IM artesunate) to get the drug into their system immediately.

question: During a vaginal examination, a midwife notices the baby's skull bones are overlapping tightly and cannot be pushed apart with a finger. How is this graded?

options.A: Grade 1 moulding
options.B: Grade 2 moulding
options.C: Grade 0 moulding
options.D: Grade 3 moulding

explanation: When the bones overlap strongly and won't budge under finger pressure, we call that Grade 3 moulding. It's an important sign that tells us to watch out for tight squeezes (cephalopelvic disproportion)!

question: What should a nursing team do if their evaluation shows a new practice didn't improve patient results?

options.A: Hide the results from management so nobody gets blamed
options.B: Reassess how it was applied or look for alternative evidence
options.C: Stop all research activities in the hospital permanently
options.D: Keep using it anyway to avoid admitting any failure

explanation: Well thought out! Science is a journey of trial and learning. If it didn't work out, we review our steps or search for a better approach.

question: Why is IEC considered a preventive approach instead of a curative one?

options.A: It focuses on changing health behaviors before sickness happens
options.B: It replaces the need for doctors and nurses in rural areas
options.C: It provides free medicines to patients inside the hospital ward
options.D: It diagnoses infectious diseases using laboratory testing

explanation: Spot on! IEC is all about stopping health problems before they even start by educating communities, rather than waiting to treat people after they fall sick.

question: How does CBR differ from traditional hospital-based psychiatric care?

options.A: CBR is managed only by foreign medical doctors
options.B: CBR delivers rehabilitation services directly within the local community setting
options.C: CBR completely prohibits the use of any pharmaceutical treatments
options.D: CBR relies exclusively on expensive imported medications

explanation: Traditional care keeps patients inside isolated facilities, whereas CBR takes services, support, and awareness right into the neighborhoods and villages where people reside. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h1)

question: Which of these habits will NOT help reduce overall inflammation in the body?

options.A: Engaging in regular exercise
options.B: Managing chronic stress levels
options.C: Eating an anti-inflammatory diet
options.D: Smoking cigarettes daily

explanation: Correct! Smoking actually ramps up inflammation and oxidative stress, whereas healthy eating, exercise, and stress control calm it down.

question: Why is patient education a powerful nursing tool against under-prescription?

options.A: It ensures patients refuse all medications to save money
options.B: It empowers patients to ask their doctors about standard therapies for their illness
options.C: It prevents doctors from making any clinical errors during visits
options.D: It teaches patients how to fill their own prescriptions at the pharmacy

explanation: Knowledge is power! When patients understand what treatments are standard for their condition, they can speak up and ask if their care plan includes them.

question: Through which main ways can toxic substances enter the human body?

options.A: Transfusion, transplantation, infusion, and dialysis
options.B: Osmosis, filtration, active transport, and diffusion
options.C: Ingestion, inhalation, dermal absorption, and injection
options.D: Circulation, respiration, digestion, and excretion

explanation: Think of the four common entries: swallowing (ingestion), breathing in (inhalation), soaking through the skin (dermal), and needles or bites (injection). You've got this!

question: What was the primary goal of early psychiatric asylums?

options.A: To isolate patients and protect public safety
options.B: To rehabilitate individuals for quick discharge
options.C: To provide advanced psychotherapy and counseling
options.D: To test new pharmaceutical medications

explanation: Early asylums functioned mainly to lock away people with mental illness to keep them out of the general community. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h2)

question: A nurse wants to find articles about asthma in children, but wants to completely leave out studies on adults. Which search string is best?

options.A: asthma NOT children AND adults
options.B: asthma AND children AND adults
options.C: asthma AND children NOT adults
options.D: asthma OR children OR adults

explanation: Using AND narrows the focus to asthma and children, while NOT removes any articles that mention adults. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is usually at the root of organizational conflict?

options.A: Patients refusing to take medication
options.B: A nurse having low self-esteem
options.C: Systemic issues and structural policies
options.D: Personal dislikes between two nurses

explanation: Organizational conflict stems from institutional rules, budgets, and structures rather than personal beefs.

question: Which bedside tool is commonly used in emergencies to quickly check for internal belly bleeding?

options.A: Electrocardiogram
options.B: FAST ultrasound
options.C: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.D: Barium swallow study

explanation: The FAST exam is a quick ultrasound used right at the bedside to spot hidden fluid or blood in trauma patients.

question: Where are Golgi tendon organs found in the body?

options.A: Inside the gray matter of the spinal cord
options.B: Deep inside the main belly of skeletal muscle fibers
options.C: At the junction where muscle fibers blend into tendons
options.D: Directly within the outer layer of the skin surface

explanation: Golgi tendon organs sit right at the meeting point where muscle fibers turn into tendons, putting them in the best spot to feel tension.

question: A nurse ignores a ward medication rule, and the patient gets hurt. What legal problem might this cause?

options.A: The hospital policy automatically protects the nurse from blame
options.B: The legal system ignores internal hospital rules completely
options.C: The policy becomes invalid because a nurse chose not to use it
options.D: The breach of policy can be used as evidence of negligence

explanation: Skipping established safety steps without a good clinical reason makes it much easier to prove a breach of duty if something goes wrong.

question: What is the main idea behind a Public-Private Partnership (PPP)?

options.A: Military defense tactics and nursing education
options.B: Traditional herbal medicine and spiritual healing
options.C: Foreign travel agencies and local pharmacies
options.D: Government authority and private sector efficiency

explanation: A PPP combines the rules and backing of the government with the speed and business skills of the private sector to get things done.

question: How do heavy seasonal rains often mess up food distribution in remote rural areas?

options.A: By instantly improving the storage life of harvested grain
options.B: By lowering the market prices of imported foods
options.C: By increasing the purchasing power of local farmers
options.D: By turning unpaved roads into mud and blocking transport trucks

explanation: When unpaved roads turn to thick mud during heavy rains, delivery trucks can't get through, cutting off remote communities. Makes total sense!

question: What does 'monitoring' primarily involve in community health programs?

options.A: Continuous tracking of service uptake and activities
options.B: Waiting until a five-year grant period finishes
options.C: Changing the geographic location of the clinic daily
options.D: Firing staff members who fail to meet quotas

explanation: Monitoring is an ongoing process of tracking day-to-day activities and service delivery metrics. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h7)

question: A patient in skin traction complains of severe leg spasms, and the nurse sees the rope is caught on the pulley wheel. What is the best first step?

options.A: Realign the rope smoothly into the center of the pulley groove
options.B: Cut the traction tape immediately to release all skin pressure
options.C: Administer a stronger pain pill and wait for relief
options.D: Raise the head of the bed high

explanation: You've got this! When a rope slips, the weights stop pulling correctly, which causes muscle spasms. Just pop the rope back into the groove to fix the tension right away.

question: Why do the kidneys often take a hit during prolonged body-wide asphyxia?

options.A: Lactic acid crystals block the small ureter tubes
options.B: They absorb too much carbon dioxide from the blood
options.C: They experience severe reduction in blood perfusion
options.D: The kidneys overproduce urine to flush out toxins

explanation: When the body runs low on oxygen, it goes into survival mode, pulling blood away from the kidneys and skin to protect the brain and heart. Sadly, this leaves the kidneys starved and vulnerable to damage.

question: What percentage range of an adolescent's daily calories should ideally come from carbohydrates?
explanation: Carbohydrates provide the primary fuel source for daily energy and should form the largest share of teen calorie intake. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h2)

question: Which local Nigerian vegetable is commonly used in soups to provide essential iron and vitamins for nursing mothers?

options.A: Raw cocoa powder
options.B: Refined white sugar
options.C: Ugu (fluted pumpkin leaves)
options.D: Dried cassava flakes

explanation: Ugu leaves are rich in iron and vital vitamins, making them a staple in local postpartum soups across Nigeria. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h6)

question: How does Maslow's hierarchy of needs apply to nursing school and patient care?

options.A: Basic survival and safety needs must be met before higher learning occurs
options.B: Classroom lectures should always focus on physical punishment
options.C: Students must memorize every medical diagnosis before touching a patient
options.D: Emotional support is completely secondary to technical skills

explanation: It's hard to focus on studying pathophysiology if you're exhausted, starving, or stressed about safety. Basic needs always come first for both students and patients!

question: How can nurses actively help prevent unsafe abortions out in the community?

options.A: By educating the public on modern contraception and reproductive health
options.B: By banning the sale of harmful chemicals in local markets
options.C: By arresting individuals who perform illegal medical procedures
options.D: By strictly refusing to treat patients who attempted self-induction

explanation: Exactly right! Community education prevents unintended pregnancies in the first place, reducing the need for dangerous, hidden procedures.

question: An adult patient with a severe disability is grimacing and pulling at their clothes during care. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: The patient is expressing boredom with the daily routine
options.B: The patient is reacting to normal room temperature changes
options.C: The patient is refusing basic hygiene for personal reasons
options.D: The patient may be experiencing untreated pain or discomfort

explanation: When patients can't easily speak, body language like grimacing or restlessness is our biggest clue that they are hurting. Trust your clinical instincts!

question: What does emotional intelligence mainly mean for a nurse leader?

options.A: Memorizing every institutional policy word for word
options.B: Understanding and managing one's own emotions while empathizing with others
options.C: Suppressing all personal feelings to maintain a strict professional exterior
options.D: Using rapid mathematical calculations to manage unit budgets

explanation: Emotional intelligence is all about self-awareness and empathy—knowing how you feel and genuinely connecting with your team's feelings too.

question: How does a nurse apply the principle of justice on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: By ignoring minor complaints from elderly clients to focus on wealthy individuals
options.B: By spending the entire shift caring only for clients who pay extra hospital fees
options.C: By providing equal and fair quality care to every assigned client regardless of background
options.D: By refusing to admit clients who belong to a different religious group

explanation: Justice means treating all clients fairly and equitably without bias or discrimination based on their social status. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h2)

question: What triggers a tapeworm cyst to release its head (scolex) once a human eats contaminated meat?

options.A: Gastric acid and enzymes digesting the cyst wall to release the scolex
options.B: Immune system suppression caused by the larval waste products
options.C: The low temperature inside the human small intestine
options.D: Direct contact with human blood cells in the mucosal lining

explanation: Exactly! Stomach acid and digestive juices break open the cyst, freeing the scolex so it can attach firmly to the small intestine.

question: Why is having a personal interest in your research topic important?

options.A: It removes the need for formal ethical approval
options.B: It makes the data analysis process completely automatic
options.C: It gives the researcher motivation to complete the demanding project
options.D: It automatically guarantees funding from the government

explanation: Research writing can get tough! Genuine curiosity and passion for your topic are what keep you going through the late nights.

question: When is home quarantine most appropriate to use during an outbreak?

options.A: When the patient has severe symptoms requiring oxygen therapy
options.B: When the individual has adequate housing and is likely to comply
options.C: When there are no family members living in the same house
options.D: When an entire city needs to be locked down immediately

explanation: Home quarantine works best when living conditions allow separation and the person agrees to stay indoors. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the single most important and effective habit for stopping infections from spreading in any hospital or clinic?

options.A: Proper hand hygiene
options.B: Wearing sterile gloves
options.C: Using N95 respirators
options.D: Isolating sick patients

explanation: Spot on! Simple, regular handwashing or hand sanitizing is your #1 defense against carrying germs from one patient to another.

question: What is a key time-based rule for diagnosing obsessive-compulsive neurosis?

options.A: Behaviors must last continuously for at least five full years
options.B: The episodes must happen only once every month without fail
options.C: The rituals must occur strictly during morning hours upon waking
options.D: Symptoms must take up more than one hour daily or cause marked distress

explanation: Correct! For a formal diagnosis, these thoughts or rituals usually need to steal over an hour of the patient's day or cause serious distress.

question: How does the Theory of Knowledge apply when a nursing team tests a new wound dressing?

options.A: They predict it will speed healing, try it on select patients, and study the actual results.
options.B: They force all patients in the hospital to use it on day one.
options.C: They assume it works because the vendor said so without checking anything.
options.D: They stop documenting wound progress because new products always work.

explanation: That's evidence-based practice in action! Predict an outcome, test it carefully, and look at the real-world data.

question: What was Paul Ehrlich searching for with his idea of a 'magic bullet'?

options.A: To invent a vaccine that prevents all known viral infections with a single dose
options.B: To find a chemical that targets and destroys pathogens while sparing the human host
options.C: To prove that bad air is the primary cause of wound infections in surgery
options.D: To design a high-powered microscope lens that magnifies living viruses

explanation: The magic bullet is all about selective toxicity—wiping out the bad germs without poisoning the patient's healthy cells.

question: What is the replacement-level fertility rate needed to keep a population stable over time?

options.A: 2.1 children per woman
options.B: 1.0 child per woman
options.C: 4.5 children per woman
options.D: 6.0 children per woman

explanation: A fertility rate of roughly 2.1 children per woman means each generation replaces itself nicely without causing the population to surge or shrink too fast.

question: What does a rust-colored sputum sample often point toward?

options.A: Simple dehydration
options.B: Severe throat irritation
options.C: Pneumococcal pneumonia
options.D: Common viral cold

explanation: Rust-colored sputum contains blood mixed with inflammatory exudate, which is typical of pneumococcal pneumonia. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h3)

question: How is drug-resistant epilepsy defined in clinical practice?

options.A: Occurrence of a single seizure during medication tapering
options.B: Inability to afford prescribed medication costs over one month
options.C: Experiencing side effects from a newly introduced drug
options.D: Failure of adequate trials of two tolerated anti-seizure medications

explanation: It's called drug-resistant when two properly chosen anti-seizure medications have been tried at good doses, but the patient still has seizures. You're mastering advanced nursing concepts!

question: Why is infection control extra important for open wounds treated out at sea?

options.A: Exposure to seawater and marine bacteria increases contamination risks.
options.B: Sunlight reflecting off water prevents wounds from closing naturally.
options.C: Shipboard water supplies are completely sterile and cause irritation.
options.D: Ocean air contains chemical toxins that dissolve human skin.

explanation: Spot on! Seawater and marine environments carry specific germs that can easily infect an open injury, making quick and clean wound care vital.

question: A care assistant is about to feed a resident who has trouble swallowing. What safety tip should you give?

options.A: Offer large chunks of solid food for better chewing
options.B: Feed the resident as quickly as possible
options.C: Position the resident in an upright sitting posture
options.D: Encourage the resident to lie flat on the bed

explanation: Brilliant! Sitting upright uses gravity to help swallowing and keeps food out of the lungs, preventing dangerous choking.

question: Why must chest compressions pause briefly when someone is giving an intracardiac injection?

options.A: To ensure the intravenous line stays securely in place
options.B: To prevent the needle from moving and tearing the heart muscle
options.C: To keep the patient from waking up during the procedure
options.D: To allow the nurse time to chart the medication administration

explanation: Safety first! CPR makes the chest bounce around, which would cause a needle inside the heart to rip the muscle tissue.

question: What term describes the guilt and emotional trauma healthcare workers feel after an adverse event?

options.A: Primary clinical burnout
options.B: Second victim syndrome
options.C: Professional apathy disorder
options.D: Acute diagnostic fatigue

explanation: We call healthcare workers 'second victims' when they suffer deep emotional distress and trauma after a clinical error.

question: What happens when data collection for a quality project takes too much nursing time?

options.A: The government awards the hospital a special safety prize
options.B: Patients begin recording their own vital signs daily
options.C: Staff may fabricate numbers just to fill out the forms
options.D: Hospital printers automatically run out of official paper

explanation: Overly burdensome data entry leads to burnout and inaccurate reporting because bedside time is precious. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of adding chlorine during water treatment?

options.A: To kill remaining pathogenic microorganisms
options.B: To settle heavy sand particles to the bottom
options.C: To make the water taste sweet and fresh
options.D: To remove dissolved iron and copper

explanation: Disinfection agents like chlorine are used at the final stages to destroy any remaining bacteria, viruses, or parasites. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h6)

question: What should be included in a good community action plan?

options.A: An order for expensive medical equipment from foreign countries
options.B: A legal contract signed by every adult living in the district
options.C: A strict list of punishments for people who refuse to participate
options.D: Clear details on who will do what, when, and with what materials

explanation: An effective plan outlines specific roles, timelines, and resources so everyone knows their responsibilities. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h5)

question: What type of tissue makes up uterine fibroids?

options.A: Stratified squamous tissue
options.B: Glandular epithelial tissue
options.C: Adipose and fibrous tissue
options.D: Smooth muscle and connective tissue

explanation: Fibroids are non-cancerous growths made of the exact same smooth muscle and connective tissue found in the muscular wall of the uterus.

question: A maternity team wants to reduce postpartum bleeding. Which option is the best, most practical aim statement?

options.A: Reduce postpartum hemorrhage rates by 30% across the maternity ward over the next four months
options.B: Ensure that all midwives are properly trained in modern obstetric emergency response techniques
options.C: Stop postpartum bleeding completely by purchasing more uterotonic drugs for the clinic
options.D: Make sure every patient giving birth receives high-quality and compassionate nursing care

explanation: A great goal is specific, easy to measure, and has a clear timeline. This option hits all three marks!

question: When do primary menstrual cramps usually hurt the most?

options.A: Exactly halfway through the normal menstrual cycle
options.B: During the first twenty-four hours of menstruation
options.C: On the final day when bleeding has nearly stopped
options.D: Two weeks before the menstrual bleeding begins

explanation: Spot on! Prostaglandin levels peak right at the start of your period, which is why the first day is usually the most painful.

question: What is the main job of antiemetic medications?

options.A: Lowering high blood glucose levels in diabetes
options.B: Preventing or relieving nausea and vomiting
options.C: Stimulating regular bowel movements
options.D: Reducing excess stomach acid production

explanation: Antiemetics target the vomiting center in the brain or gut to help settle an upset stomach and stop vomiting.

question: What tool can nurses use to help patients estimate portion sizes more accurately?

options.A: A standard household measuring cup for liquid medications only
options.B: A complex laboratory blood test for vitamin levels
options.C: Visual aids like food models or picture charts
options.D: Strict financial receipts from local grocery stores

explanation: Patients often struggle to describe portion sizes in grams or cups, so visual aids make it easier for them to show how much they ate. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h8)

question: Which of these nursing examples uses a quantitative design?

options.A: Recording a journal of daily emotional struggles during grief counseling
options.B: Observing nurse-patient interactions during a busy ward handover
options.C: Measuring hourly blood sugar levels after giving a new insulin dose
options.D: Interviewing elderly patients about their childhood memories of illness

explanation: Tracking blood sugar gives you clear numbers that you can run statistics on—that is the classic sign of quantitative research.

question: Which professional primarily helps a special child improve fine motor skills for daily tasks like dressing and eating?

options.A: Speech-language pathologist
options.B: Pharmacist
options.C: Occupational therapist
options.D: Physiotherapist

explanation: Occupational therapists focus on upper body function and fine motor tasks needed for everyday independence. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is the main job of endocrine glands in our body?

options.A: Filtering waste products out of liquid blood
options.B: Secreting hormones directly into the bloodstream
options.C: Producing digestive enzymes for the stomach
options.D: Pumping oxygenated blood to body tissues

explanation: Spot on! Endocrine glands don't use ducts. They release their chemical messengers (hormones) straight into nearby blood vessels to reach organs all over the body.

question: Which action shows safe, ethical nursing practice regarding alternative treatments?

options.A: Prescribing high-dose vitamins without checking laboratory values
options.B: Evaluating scientific evidence while keeping communication open with the patient
options.C: Mocking the patient for believing in natural healing methods
options.D: Pretending alternative treatments do not exist at all

explanation: Good nursing means keeping an open, non-judgmental dialogue so patients feel safe sharing what they take, while we check the facts.

question: A nurse is caring for a patient receiving an infusion of oxytocin to stimulate labor contractions. Which risk requires the nurse to monitor this patient most closely?

options.A: Severe fetal distress from hyperstimulation
options.B: Sudden vision loss and chronic migraines
options.C: Total paralysis of the lower extremities
options.D: Sudden development of adult asthma

explanation: Oxytocin is a high-alert drug that causes uterine contractions; too much medicine can cause contractions that are too strong or frequent, cutting off oxygen to the baby. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h2)

question: A patient takes their normal drug, but after drinking a lot of an enzyme-inhibiting juice, they show signs of drug toxicity. What happened?

options.A: The juice physically destroyed the kidneys so they could not produce urine
options.B: The juice increased the number of liver enzymes so the drug worked too fast
options.C: The juice slowed down the drug's metabolism, causing it to build up in the blood
options.D: The juice acted as a prodrug and converted the medication into a poison

explanation: Inhibition puts the brakes on metabolic enzymes. Because the drug can't break down normally, it accumulates in the bloodstream until it reaches toxic levels. Great clinical insight to know!

question: Which category of healthcare waste includes discarded scalpels and broken glass ampoules?

options.A: Sharps
options.B: Pharmaceutical waste
options.C: Pathological waste
options.D: General waste

explanation: Sharps are any objects that can puncture or cut skin, including needles, surgical blades, and broken glass vials. [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h2)

question: Where does spermatogenesis actually take place inside the testes?

options.A: In the tunica albuginea
options.B: In the vas deferens
options.C: In the seminiferous tubules
options.D: In the prostate gland

explanation: The tightly coiled seminiferous tubules form the structural foundation where sperm cells are actively produced. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the key target recommended by the Abuja Declaration for national health budgets?

options.A: Less than 5% of annual tax revenue
options.B: At least 15% of the national budget
options.C: Zero government spending on clinics
options.D: Exactly 50% of all foreign aid

explanation: The Abuja Declaration urged African governments to allocate a minimum of 15% of their annual budgets to improve the health sector. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a warning sign of worsening breathing trouble that patients should watch out for at home?

options.A: Increasing swelling in the lower limbs
options.B: Improved appetite and steady weight gain
options.C: Inability to speak in full sentences
options.D: Blue discoloration around the lips

explanation: Eating well and gaining steady weight are signs of recovery! The other options show the patient is getting worse and needs help urgently.

question: Why should nurses avoid using judgmental words in patient notes (like 'uncooperative' or 'difficult')?

options.A: They stop the clinic from sending electronic government reports.
options.B: They automatically make the patient chart illegal in court.
options.C: They are unprofessional, biased, and do not provide clear factual evidence of patient status.
options.D: They take up too much physical writing space in the register.

explanation: Stick to the facts! Writing what you actually see and hear ('patient refused medication') is much more professional and legally safe than adding personal opinions.

question: What does 'maladministration' mean in a public healthcare setting?

options.A: Providing free medications to every patient who visits the emergency ward
options.B: Failure to act properly, unreasonable delays, or unfairness in service delivery
options.C: Achieving all hospital targets ahead of the scheduled fiscal deadline
options.D: Conducting thorough and regular audits of hospital financial accounts

explanation: Maladministration covers poor governance—think unfair treatment, unnecessary delays, negligence, or corrupt practices in running the facility.

question: Why is it beneficial to involve local community leaders in disaster awareness programs?

options.A: They dictate government policy changes during emergencies
options.B: They possess specialized degrees in disaster management
options.C: They are legally required to fund all local health clinics
options.D: They help build trust and ensure the message resonates with residents

explanation: Local leaders have established relationships with residents, making it easier for the community to accept safety advice. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T9#GNS315_U5_T9_h4)

question: Why is primary health care considered the bedrock of a solid health system?

options.A: It focuses solely on emergency trauma surgeries
options.B: It is funded entirely by international donors rather than local governments
options.C: It eliminates the need for any specialized doctors or hospitals
options.D: It prevents minor health issues from becoming major hospital burdens by catching them early

explanation: By offering promotive and preventive services early at the community level, PHC stops health problems from escalating. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h1)

question: When auditors talk about the 'scope' of a management audit, what do they mean?

options.A: The exact amount of salary each nurse will receive
options.B: The architectural design of the hospital building
options.C: The boundaries and specific departments to be examined
options.D: The schedule for routine patient visiting hours

explanation: The scope simply sets the boundaries—it tells the audit team which exact units, departments, or processes they need to look into so they don't get overwhelmed.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical result of eating a lot of junk food or processed snacks during adolescence?

options.A: Poor long-term bone health
options.B: Stronger skeletal bone density
options.C: Increased risk of iron deficiency
options.D: Erratic eating schedules

explanation: Processed foods lack key nutrients like calcium, so they certainly won't build stronger bones!

question: Why would a dietitian need to check laboratory test results during a patient assessment?

options.A: To spot hidden signs of malnutrition or metabolic imbalance
options.B: To calculate the exact cost of hospital food supplies
options.C: To diagnose infectious diseases independent of a doctor
options.D: To determine when a patient is ready for physical therapy

explanation: You got it! Lab values like albumin and blood glucose give clear, objective proof of how well a patient's body is handling nutrients.

question: What does the term 'brain drain' mean for Nigerian healthcare?

options.A: The gradual loss of memory in elderly psychiatric patients
options.B: A neurological disease caused by severe vitamin deficiencies in adults
options.C: The closure of mental health training schools due to lack of students
options.D: The mass emigration of skilled health workers leaving facilities understaffed

explanation: Correct! Brain drain refers to trained professionals leaving the country for better opportunities abroad, which leaves our remaining hospitals and clinics understaffed.

question: In the PQRST pain assessment tool, what does the letter 'Q' stand for?

options.A: Quietness
options.B: Quickness
options.C: Quality
options.D: Quantity

explanation: Great job! 'Q' stands for Quality. It means asking the patient to describe what the pain feels like—is it sharp, dull, stabbing, or throbbing?

question: In healthcare, what does the abbreviation MHPSS stand for?

options.A: Mental Hygiene and Psychological Support System
options.B: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support
options.C: Medical Hospital Psychiatric Safety Service
options.D: Multidisciplinary Health Practice and Social Studies

explanation: You'll see MHPSS a lot in nursing! It’s the standard term for programs that care for people's emotional and social needs, especially during crises.

question: What is your main job as the nurse while the doctor performs a thoracentesis?

options.A: Reading the final lab results before fluid collection
options.B: Inserting the drainage catheter into the pleural cavity
options.C: Administering general anesthesia through an IV line
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and watching for signs of distress

explanation: Exactly right! Your eyes are on the patient—keep a close check on their breathing, heart rate, and comfort while the fluid drains.

question: Which layer of the skin has the highest number of specialized touch receptors?

options.A: Dermis
options.B: Stratum corneum
options.C: Epidermis
options.D: Subcutaneous adipose

explanation: Great job! The dermis sits right beneath the outer layer and houses most of those complex touch and pressure receptors.

question: How do sudden altitude changes during an air medical evacuation affect a patient?

options.A: They instantly lower the patient's core body temperature
options.B: They prevent intravenous pumps from delivering fluids
options.C: They completely eliminate the risk of internal bleeding
options.D: They cause trapped gases inside body cavities to expand

explanation: As the plane climbs and air pressure drops, any trapped air inside the body—like in the gut or middle ear—expands just like a bag of chips at high altitude!

question: Which of the following is a common positive result of using person-centered care?

options.A: Decreased staffing requirements across all shifts
options.B: Shorter hospital stays for acute trauma patients
options.C: Reduced behavioral symptoms in residents with dementia
options.D: Elimination of the need for any medication administration

explanation: Spot on! When patients feel heard, respected, and comfortable, it often lowers anxiety and reduces challenging behaviors in dementia.

question: Roughly what percentage of patients with full Korsakoff syndrome make a complete recovery?

options.A: Zero percent
options.B: Exactly 75 percent
options.C: Nearly 90 percent
options.D: About 20 percent

explanation: Only a small fraction (around one in five) recover fully, which is why catching and treating early Wernicke signs is so important!

question: During a traditional diaphragm fitting, what two points does the nurse measure between?

options.A: Clitoris to the perineal body
options.B: Posterior fornix to the pubic bone
options.C: Cervical os to the vaginal introitus
options.D: Uterine fundus to the pelvic inlet

explanation: To get the right size, clinicians measure from the back of the vagina (posterior fornix) to the back of the pubic bone.

question: What is the main reason we use the ABCDEF protocol in emergency care?

options.A: To document nursing care for legal cover
options.B: To figure out the final medical diagnosis
options.C: To replace the need for lab tests
options.D: To find and treat life-threatening problems step-by-step

explanation: You've got this! The ABCDEF guide helps healthcare teams tackle the scariest, most immediate life threats first so nothing gets missed. Great job thinking like an emergency nurse!

question: How do changing body shapes during pregnancy typically affect a woman's body image?

options.A: They invariably cause permanent clinical body dysmorphia
options.B: They produce mixed responses ranging from empowerment to distress
options.C: They have zero emotional impact on the expectant mother
options.D: They universally improve self-esteem across all trimesters

explanation: Every woman is different! Some love their glowing bump while others struggle with the physical changes, and both reactions are valid.

question: What is the final organ responsible for turning vitamin D into its active hormonal form, calcitriol?

options.A: Stomach
options.B: Liver
options.C: Skin
options.D: Kidneys

explanation: The kidneys perform the final activation step on vitamin D so the body can properly absorb calcium. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T8#GNS121_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which traditional practice is strictly prohibited by the VAPP Act?

options.A: Traditional naming ceremonies
options.B: Female genital mutilation
options.C: Community farming festivals
options.D: Age-grade cultural dances

explanation: That's correct! Practices like female genital mutilation (FGM) and harmful widowhood rites are explicitly outlawed by the VAPP Act.

question: What is the main goal of community mobilisation in health care?

options.A: Replacing traditional healers with foreign nurses
options.B: Building more hospitals in urban centres
options.C: Bringing people together to take joint action for health
options.D: Training only doctors to run local clinics

explanation: Community mobilisation is fundamentally about uniting individuals and groups to tackle common health issues together. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which key principle says that local people must be involved in planning their own health programs?

options.A: Rigid institutional control
options.B: Private medical practice
options.C: Hospital confinement
options.D: Active participation

explanation: Great job! Health programs work best when community members roll up their sleeves and take part right from the planning stage.

question: Why is partner notification and treatment a must when managing STIs?

options.A: To punish individuals who engage in unprotected sexual intercourse
options.B: To determine which partner originally contracted the infection first
options.C: To prevent reinfection and break the ongoing cycle of transmission
options.D: To fulfill mandatory insurance reporting requirements for hospitals

explanation: If you treat only one partner, they will just catch the infection right back the next time they have sex. Both partners must be treated together to truly heal!

question: What is the best way for a nurse to prevent falls in a hospital ward?

options.A: Keeping all side rails locked in the fully raised position
options.B: Conducting individual risk assessments and targeted interventions
options.C: Removing call bells so patients do not attempt to get up alone
options.D: Restricting all patients to strict bed rest throughout their stay

explanation: Every patient is different! Assessing each person's unique fall risks and tailoring care to them works much better than locking everyone in bed.

question: Which term describes a dispute happening between the Emergency Department and the Surgical Ward?

options.A: Intergroup conflict
options.B: Intragroup conflict
options.C: Intrapersonal conflict
options.D: Internalized conflict

explanation: When two separate teams or departments lock horns, it's called intergroup conflict. 'Inter' means between different groups!

question: In maternal health, what does 'morbidity' mean?

options.A: The death of a woman while pregnant or within forty-two days of delivery
options.B: The total number of pregnant women admitted to a tertiary hospital
options.C: Any infection contracted by a newborn baby during the first week of life
options.D: Any health condition caused or worsened by pregnancy and childbirth

explanation: Think of morbidity simply as the illnesses, injuries, or health struggles that happen because of pregnancy—distinct from maternal mortality, which means death. You've got this!

question: A discharged patient calls saying they notice red streaks spreading up their arm from a dog bite. What should the nurse advise?

options.A: Apply an ice pack and wait another forty-eight hours
options.B: Stop taking the antibiotics because the red streaks are normal
options.C: Wash the arm with scented soap and increase fluid intake
options.D: Return to the emergency department immediately for evaluation

explanation: Spreading red streaks suggest a fast-moving infection like lymphangitis. This requires prompt medical re-evaluation right away!

question: Why is just smelling food a poor way to tell if it is safe to eat?

options.A: Sniffing food exposes your lungs to dangerous kitchen fumes.
options.B: Harmful food poisoning bacteria often do not change how food smells or looks.
options.C: Spoiled food always smells sweet instead of sour.
options.D: Human noses cannot detect any bad odors coming from spoiled meat.

explanation: Dangerous germs can hide in food without changing its scent or look at all. Always check expiry dates and store food safely!

question: Why should a nurse check a patient's serum albumin lab result before giving a protein-bound drug?

options.A: To measure the exact body fat percentage
options.B: To see how well the kidneys are making urine
options.C: To determine if there is a bacterial infection
options.D: To check if the patient is at risk for drug toxicity

explanation: Low albumin levels change the balance of bound vs. free drug. Checking this lab value helps you keep the patient safe from unexpected high doses of active medicine.
